title: Platform checks (contract v2)
description: Written by the runner to /trial/out/checks.json after every trial (evals_adapter.checks), never by the adapter. Number provenance: every money amount the agent wrote, and how it was verified (D61, 5 Nov): it matches a tool result, the task's client file or a user message at the precision shown (source), or the result of an arithmetic call that counts (tool), or the checker recomputes it as a one-step derivation from those with at least one sourced amount (derived_in_prose); else it is unsupported. Required tool calls: which of the task's required_tools the agent called. Heuristics for a reader and a grader primitive, not a grade. See docs/adapter-contract.md section 12. The fields marked D56 were added on 5 Nov and are optional here, so a checks.json written before them still validates; the runner always writes them now.

amounts.description: Every money amount in the agent's replies, in order: ₹, Rs, INR or 'rupees' amounts, lakh and crore forms, and Indian digit grouping from one lakh up.

turn.description: The agent turn the reply belongs to, from 0.

text.description: The amount as written, such as '₹4.41 lakh'.

supported_by.description: Where a matching number was: a tool result (tool), the task's client file (client), or a user or simulated-client message (user); `derived` (D61) when the checker recomputed it as a one-step derivation (see `derivation`); null when it is unsupported. An arithmetic tool's result is a tool source only when `arithmetic` accepts its call (D56).

verified_by.description: D61: source (it matches a non-arithmetic tool result, the client file or a message), tool (the result of an arithmetic call that counts), derived_in_prose (the checker recomputed it: written without a tool) or null (unsupported). Absent before D61.

derivation.description: D61: null unless verified_by is derived_in_prose: the derivation the checker found.

rejected.description: D56: null unless the amount has no source and matched an arithmetic result that does not count: the best such match, and the call's reason from `arithmetic`.

unsupported.description: How many amounts have supported_by null.

derived_in_prose.description: D61: how many amounts were verified only as a derivation the checker recomputed, i.e. written without a tool. Absent before D61.

tools_called.description: Every tool the agent called, once each, in first-call order, with harness prefixes removed (Hermes's mcp__finance__).

required_tools.description: Null when the task lists no required_tools.

called.description: Required tools with at least one execute_tool span.

only_errors.description: Called required tools whose every call returned an error.

arithmetic.description: D56: every call of an arithmetic tool (add, subtract, multiply, divide, percent_of, percent_change, round), in start order, and whether its result counts as a source. It counts only when the call returned no error, was given at least one number, and every number it was given (round's places aside) matches, by the same rule as an amount, an earlier non-arithmetic tool result or accepted arithmetic result, the client file, or a user message up to the call's turn, or (D58, 5 Nov) is a unit fact. Since D61 an input may also be a free factor or a one-step derivation of sourced numbers; add, subtract, percent_change and round need a source for every input, and every call needs one sourced amount (100 or more). Even then it does not count when a number in its result only repeats an input that has no source (D58's identity guard). Absent from a checks.json written before D56, which did not trace arithmetic inputs.

tool.description: The tool, with harness prefixes removed.

turn.description: The agent turn the call belongs to, from 0; -1 when its span has no turn parent.

supported.description: Whether the call's result counts as a source.

inputs.description: Every number the call was given, in argument order.

arg.description: The argument it was given in: values[0], a, value.

value.description: The number as given; null for NaN or an infinity.

supported_by.description: Where a matching number was, as for an amount; `unit` (D58, 5 Nov) when nothing matched but the input is a unit fact (7, 12, 28 to 31, 52, 100, 365, 366, 1,00,000 or 1,00,00,000, sign ignored), which needs no source; `free` (D61) for another free factor (a whole number from 1 to 60, or a percentage written in the replies); `derived` (D61) when it is a one-step derivation of sourced numbers. `match` is null for all three.

derivation.description: D61: present when supported_by is derived.

reason.description: Null when the result counts; else why not: "add's input 12,345 is not supported", "round returned an error", "divide's arguments could not be read", "round's result 365 only repeats its input 365, which has no source" (D58).

derivation.description: D61: a one-step derivation the checker recomputed: op on the operands gives value, which matches the figure as `how` says.

op.description: add, subtract, multiply, divide, percent_of (a x b / 100), sum (a run of figures in the reply) or repeat (a figure derived earlier).

where.description: Where the operand came from: tool:<name>, client:<file>, <source>:<index> for a message, answer:<turn> for a figure verified in a reply, count, unit fact, or answer % for a percentage written in the replies.

call.description: D56: a tool call's position among the trial's tool calls (its execute_tool spans in start order), from 0.

how.description: exact; rounded half-up to the precision shown (or at trailing zeros, within 1%); truncated to the precision shown.

where.description: tool:<tool name>, client:<file name>, or <source>:<transcript index> for a message (task:0, client_sim:2).

precision.description: The step the amount was compared at, in rupees: 0.01 for '₹8,997.26', 1000 for '₹4.41 lakh'.

reason.description: Why that result is not a source, such as "add's input 12,345 is not supported".
